subject: Nimbus Health — HSM escrow & audit retention billing alternatives
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@nimbushealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Andrews <t.andrews@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HSM escrow + audit retention billing model

Rafael,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we discussed on the RFP, Nimbus is evaluating two procurement avenues: a capitalized, one-time escrow for HSM appliances and a predictable recurring charge for audit-log retention. Procurement is pushing back on the standard per-seat HSM license model because we onboard multiple datacenter regions and need a billing approach that maps to our internal CAPEX/OPEX lines.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood split the HSM charge into a one-time escrow (hardware-bound) + a smaller recurring security service fee?
- Can audit log retention be tiered (30/90/365 days) with consumption-based overage rather than a flat high-retention premium?
- Any concessions on implementation/setup fees if we commit to a 36-month Dedicated + Private deployment?

I attached the HSM requirements from our security team for reference (Nimbus_RFP_HSM_requirements.pdf). Looking for a proposal by EOD Friday so we can include it in our sourcing packet.

Best,
Emma Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health

--
Attachment: Nimbus_RFP_HSM_requirements.pdf (pdf, 312 KB)
From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Tom Andrews <t.andrews@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HSM escrow + audit retention billing model

Emma —

Appreciate the clear ask and the RFP doc. I've sketched three pragmatic billing paths (attached as Proposed_Billing_worksheet.xlsx) that aim to meet Nimbus's CAPEX/OPEX separation while preserving Redwood's operational guarantees. Short summary below; full numbers in the worksheet.

Option A — Seat-focused (baseline)
- One-time HSM provisioning fee (covers HSM seats, KMS integration, initial key import).
- Recurring per-active-seat license for HSM usage.
- Audit retention premium flat fee for >90d.
- Good if you need per-region isolation and predictable per-seat SLAs.

Option B — Escrow + Security Service (recommended for procurement)
- One-time escrow/escrow-equivalent payment that covers physical HSM provisioning and HSM appliance scheduling across datacenters. (Amortized across 36 months for internal accounting if you prefer.)
- Lower monthly security service fee (includes key rotation, backup, limited on-call support).
- Audit logs: base 30d included; tiered add-on for 90d/365d with metered overage (GB/month) rather than a flat premium.
- We can offer a limited implementation fee credit ($30k) if you commit to 36 months of Dedicated + Private.

Option C — Pure Opex (usage-first)
- No upfront escrow; higher monthly security service + per-HSM-hour billing for peak provisioning.
- Audit retention fully metered.
- Lower commitment but higher unit cost.

Risks/notes:
- Escrow payments are refundable upon termination with a 6-month pro-rata schedule; we'll need standard custodial terms in the SOW.
- HSM appliances for on-prem/private deployments still require coordination with your infra team for physical handoff windows.

Next steps: Laura (cc'd) from our finance team can confirm the amortization language and final margin on Option B. If Option B looks good, I can create a redlineable addendum for procurement and a DocuSign package for PO acceptance.

Thanks — attaching the worksheet.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachments: Proposed_Billing_worksheet.xlsx (xlsx, 48 KB)
From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: HSM escrow + audit retention billing model — need pricing confirmation

LAURA / BEN —

Forwarding Nimbus's ask and my initial options. Procurement is explicitly requesting an escrow-style treatment for HSMs and a metered model for audit retention; they prefer Option B but will look to negotiate escrow amortization and implementation credit.

Can you confirm quickly:
1) Is a $30k implementation credit (applied over first three invoices) acceptable given a 36-month Dedicated+Private commit for the NIM-2317 deal?
2) Can finance draft sample SOW language for escrow refund schedule (6-month pro-rata) and custodial responsibilities?
3) From a product/support POV: what SLAs do we guarantee for HSM failover across regions if escrowed? Need a short paragraph to include in the addendum.

If you want to sync 30m today I can share the worksheet live. Procurement needs a paper option by Friday.

Thanks,
Rafael

--
Internal note: worksheet shows ~15% blended margin reduction under Option B; implementation credit paid back via higher monthly ARR over the commit term.
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@nimbushealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Andrews <t.andrews@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-10-22T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HSM escrow + audit retention billing model

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear options and for pulling the worksheet together. Nimbus's exec procurement council reviewed Option B and we are prepared to move forward on that path pending two clarifications:

1) Escrow amortization: we prefer escrow treated as CAPEX with a 36-month straight-line amortization on our side; Redwood's refund schedule (6-month pro-rata) is acceptable as long as the SOW includes a clause that refunds are calculated net of any outstanding support credits.

2) Audit retention metering: confirm overage rates (per-GB/month) and whether inbound ingestion during retention window is included in overage buckets.

If you can confirm those two points and send a DocuSign-ready addendum and PO/payment instructions, procurement will route for signature. Happy to accept the $30k implementation credit in exchange for the 36-month commit.

Best,
Emma Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health
